common_meaning: Plural of that: referring to people or things at a distance, or already mentioned.
example: Those shoes by the door are mine.
rrgm_bridge: Those points outward to a group set apart from the speaker, in space, time or discussion.
invariant_mi: A plural demonstrative pointing to referents distant from the speaker or previously identified.

domain_entries.LIN: Demonstrative determiner and pronoun, plural of "that"; contrasts with "these".

count_condition: A plural referent that is distant or already introduced.
transfer_boundary: "Those people" can be used to distance or other a group; the pointing word can carry a judgement.

common_meaning: On or during this present day; also in the present period.
example: I have to finish the report today; young people today use phones for everything.
rrgm_bridge: Today is the present day, the one unit of time in which action can still be taken.
invariant_mi: The current day, or the present era.

domain_entries.LIN: Deictic: what "today" refers to depends on when it is said.
domain_entries.DIG: For a system without a clock, "today" has to be supplied from outside; it cannot be inferred from training alone.

count_condition: The day on which the speaker speaks, or the present age.
transfer_boundary: "Today" in a written record means the day it was written, not the day it is read. Statements about "people today" are generalisations.

common_meaning: Despite the fact that; however; nevertheless.
example: Though it was raining, we went for a walk.
rrgm_bridge: Though holds two facts together, one of which might have prevented the other, and lets both stand.
invariant_mi: Introduces a concession: a fact that runs against the main claim without cancelling it.

domain_entries.LIN: Conjunction ("though it rained") and adverb ("it was good, though").
domain_entries.FOR: Concession: both clauses are asserted; the contrast is between expectation and outcome.

count_condition: Two statements in tension, both held true.
transfer_boundary: A concession does not weaken the main claim; it admits a fact that might have been expected to.

common_meaning: To make an effort to do something; to test something to see if it works or is good; also to put someone on trial.
example: Try the new recipe; I tried to call but there was no answer.
rrgm_bridge: To try is to act without a guaranteed outcome: the effort is real whether or not it lands.
invariant_mi: To make an attempt, or to test.

domain_entries.COG: Trial and error: trying, observing, adjusting.
domain_entries.FOR: A trial run tests a method before committing to it.
domain_entries.REL: Being tried in court; and "trying" someone's patience.

count_condition: An effort or test whose outcome is uncertain.
transfer_boundary: Trying is not succeeding, and failing after trying is not the same as not trying. Being tried in court is not being found guilty.

common_meaning: Coming after the second in order; also one of three equal parts.
example: She finished third; a third of the class was absent.
rrgm_bridge: Third is the first position past a pair, where a new perspective can stand outside the two.
invariant_mi: The ordinal number corresponding to three, or one of three equal parts.

domain_entries.REL: A third party stands outside a two-sided relation and may mediate, judge or be affected.

count_condition: The position after second, or one part in three.
transfer_boundary: A third party is outside the relation, not neutral by default.
